title: The Fax Machine Is Older Than the Telephone

scenes.text: The fax machine was invented before the telephone.
In eighteen forty-three, a Scottish clockmaker named Alexander Bain patented a device that could send a picture down a wire.
Two swinging pendulums scanned the image line by line, and the copy appeared on chemically treated paper at the other end.
The telephone? Alexander Graham Bell did not patent it until eighteen seventy-six. Thirty-three years later.
It worked because the electric telegraph already existed. Sending pulses down a wire was old news. Sending a voice was the hard part.
So pictures were travelling down wires before the light bulb, before the typewriter, before the American Civil War. Which invention do you think is older than it looks?

description:
The fax machine was invented before the telephone.
Alexander Bain patented his image-sending telegraph in 1843, using synchronised pendulums to scan a picture line by line. Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent came 33 years later, in 1876.
It was possible because the electric telegraph already existed; sending pulses down a wire was easy compared with sending a voice.
Which invention do you think is older than it looks?
